meaning: to agree to take or receive something
tip: Accept starts with "ac" like "acquire" (you take something). Except starts with "ex" like "exclude" (you leave something out).

meaning: not including
tip: Accept starts with "ac" like "acquire" (you take something). Except starts with "ex" like "exclude" (you leave something out).

meaning: in fact, really
example: Actually, I'm from Canada, not the US.
tip: Actually means "in fact". Currently means "now". (In Spanish, French and other languages, a similar word means "now", which is why learners mix them up.)

meaning: now, at the present time
tip: Actually means "in fact". Currently means "now". (In Spanish, French and other languages, a similar word means "now", which is why learners mix them up.)

meaning: an opinion about what someone should do
example: Can I give you some advice?
tip: Advice (with c) is the noun, like "ice". Advise (with s) is the verb, and the s sounds like z.

meaning: to tell someone what you think they should do
example: I advise you to see a doctor.
tip: Advice (with c) is the noun, like "ice". Advise (with s) is the verb, and the s sounds like z.

meaning: to change or influence something
example: The cold weather affects my knees.
tip: Affect is the Action (a verb); Effect is the End result (a noun). If you can put "the" or "an" before it, you need effect.

meaning: a result or change caused by something
tip: Affect is the Action (a verb); Effect is the End result (a noun). If you can put "the" or "an" before it, you need effect.

meaning: without other people
tip: Alone is a fact (no one is with you). Lonely is a feeling (you are sad about it). You can be alone and happy.

meaning: unhappy because you are alone
example: He felt lonely in the new city.
tip: Alone is a fact (no one is with you). Lonely is a feeling (you are sad about it). You can be alone and happy.

meaning: before now, or sooner than expected
tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

meaning: until now (in questions and negatives)
tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

meaning: continuing, not finished
tip: Already = it happened (maybe early). Yet = we're waiting for it (questions and negatives, at the end). Still = it continues.

meaning: to help someone
tip: Attend = be present at (attend a class). Assist = help. (Learners who speak Spanish or French often say "assist a class" by mistake.)

meaning: to go to an event or place
tip: Attend = be present at (attend a class). Assist = help. (Learners who speak Spanish or French often say "assist a class" by mistake.)

meaning: next to, at the side of
tip: Beside = by the side of (place). Besides (with s) = plus, also.

meaning: in addition to, or also
tip: Beside = by the side of (place). Besides (with s) = plus, also.

meaning: in the space separating two (or a few clearly separate) things
example: The bank is between the café and the hotel.
tip: Between for separate, named things (between you and me). Among for a group or crowd (among the students).

meaning: in the middle of, or part of a group
tip: Between for separate, named things (between you and me). Among for a group or crowd (among the students).

meaning: feeling tired and unhappy because nothing interests you
tip: -ed describes how a person feels (bored). -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling (boring).

meaning: not interesting
tip: -ed describes how a person feels (bored). -ing describes the thing that causes the feeling (boring).

meaning: to take something that you will give back
tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends something TO you. Borrow = take, lend = give.

meaning: to give something that will be given back to you
example: Can you lend me your pen?
tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends something TO you. Borrow = take, lend = give.

meaning: to carry something toward the speaker or the place you're talking about
example: Bring your swimsuit when you come.
tip: Bring = toward here. Take = away from here to there.

meaning: to carry something away from the speaker to another place
example: Take an umbrella when you go out.
tip: Bring = toward here. Take = away from here to there.

meaning: to look at something to see if it is correct or safe
tip: Check = look and verify. Control = have power over. (Learners often say "control" when they mean "check", for example at an airport.)

meaning: to have power over something, or make it do what you want
tip: Check = look and verify. Control = have power over. (Learners often say "control" when they mean "check", for example at an airport.)

meaning: to move toward the speaker or the listener
tip: Come = toward me or you. Go = to another place. "I'm coming!" means "I'm moving toward you."

meaning: to move away from the speaker to another place
tip: Come = toward me or you. Go = to another place. "I'm coming!" means "I'm moving toward you."

meaning: something that goes well with something else
tip: A complement completes something (both have "comple"). A compliment is nice to hear (I like compliments).

meaning: something nice you say about someone
tip: A complement completes something (both have "comple"). A compliment is nice to hear (I like compliments).

meaning: to break or spoil a thing
tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

meaning: to hurt a person or animal, or have a bad effect
tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

meaning: to hurt a person's or animal's body, usually in an accident
example: She injured her knee playing soccer.
tip: Damage things (a car, a house). Injure bodies (an arm, a person in an accident). Harm is general: health, people, the environment.

meaning: at some time within a period, or through all of it
example: I fell asleep during the movie.
tip: For answers "how long?" (for two hours). During answers "when?" (during the meeting).

meaning: showing how long something lasts
example: I lived there for three years.
tip: For answers "how long?" (for two hours). During answers "when?" (during the meeting).

meaning: about the economy or money
example: The country is in an economic crisis.
tip: Economic is about the economy. Economical is about saving money: an economical car uses little fuel.

meaning: not using much money, fuel or time
tip: Economic is about the economy. Economical is about saving money: an economical car uses little fuel.

meaning: to leave your country to live in another
tip: Emigrate = Exit your country (emigrate from). Immigrate = come In (immigrate to).

meaning: to come into a new country to live
tip: Emigrate = Exit your country (emigrate from). Immigrate = come In (immigrate to).

meaning: to make certain that something happens
example: Please ensure the door is locked.
tip: Insure is about insurance (both start with "insur"). Ensure means make sure.

meaning: to buy insurance for something
tip: Insure is about insurance (both start with "insur"). Ensure means make sure.

meaning: above all, more than others
tip: Especially = particularly, most of all. Specially = for one special purpose (specially made, specially designed).

meaning: for a special purpose
example: This cake was specially made for you.
tip: Especially = particularly, most of all. Specially = for one special purpose (specially made, specially designed).

meaning: feeling happy and enthusiastic
example: The kids are excited about the trip.
tip: -ed is how you feel (excited). -ing is what makes you feel it (exciting).

meaning: causing excitement
tip: -ed is how you feel (excited). -ing is what makes you feel it (exciting).

meaning: at a greater physical distance
example: The hotel is farther than I thought.
tip: Farther is about physical distance (it has "far" in it). Further is for more of something: further information, further discussion.

meaning: more, additional, or to a greater degree
example: Do you have any further questions?
tip: Farther is about physical distance (it has "far" in it). Further is for more of something: further information, further discussion.

meaning: a smaller number of (countable nouns)
tip: Fewer for things you can count (fewer people). Less for things you can't count (less water, less time).

meaning: a smaller amount of (uncountable nouns)
tip: Fewer for things you can count (fewer people). Less for things you can't count (less water, less time).

meaning: enjoyable, or enjoyment
tip: Fun = you enjoy it. Funny = it makes you laugh (or it's strange).

meaning: making you laugh, or strange
tip: Fun = you enjoy it. Funny = it makes you laugh (or it's strange).

meaning: difficult, or with a lot of effort
tip: Hard (adverb) = with effort. Hardly = almost not. "He works hard" and "He hardly works" mean opposite things!

meaning: almost not
tip: Hard (adverb) = with effort. Hardly = almost not. "He works hard" and "He hardly works" mean opposite things!

meaning: to notice sounds with your ears
tip: You hear without trying; you listen on purpose. Listen needs "to" before an object.

meaning: to pay attention to sounds on purpose
tip: You hear without trying; you listen on purpose. Listen needs "to" before an object.

meaning: important in history
tip: Historic = famous or important (a historic day). Historical = connected with the past (a historical film).

meaning: about the past, or based on history
tip: Historic = famous or important (a historic day). Historical = connected with the past (a historical film).

meaning: to suggest something without saying it directly
tip: The speaker implies; the listener infers. Imply sends the message, infer receives it.

meaning: to reach a conclusion from information
example: What can we infer from the data?
tip: The speaker implies; the listener infers. Imply sends the message, infer receives it.

meaning: wanting to know more about something
tip: You are interested IN something; the thing is interesting.

meaning: holding your attention
tip: You are interested IN something; the thing is interesting.

meaning: belonging to it
tip: It's always means "it is" or "it has". Possessive its has no apostrophe, just like his and hers.

meaning: short for "it is" or "it has"
tip: It's always means "it is" or "it has". Possessive its has no apostrophe, just like his and hers.

meaning: the regular paid position you have
tip: Job is countable (a job, two jobs). Work as a noun is uncountable (a lot of work, not "a work").

meaning: activity you do to earn money or achieve something; the place you work
example: I have a lot of work today.
tip: Job is countable (a job, two jobs). Work as a noun is uncountable (a lot of work, not "a work").

meaning: final, or the one before now
example: This is the last bus tonight.
tip: Latest = newest (there may be more later). Last = final (no more after it), or the one before now.

meaning: the newest or most recent
example: Have you seen her latest movie?
tip: Latest = newest (there may be more later). Last = final (no more after it), or the one before now.

meaning: after the expected time
tip: Late = not on time. Lately = recently (often with the present perfect).

meaning: recently
tip: Late = not on time. Lately = recently (often with the present perfect).

meaning: to be in a flat position (no object); past: lay, lain
tip: Lay needs an object: you lay something down. Lie has no object: you lie down. The confusing part: the past of lie is lay.

meaning: to put something down flat (needs an object); past: laid
example: Lay the baby on the bed.
tip: Lay needs an object: you lay something down. Lie has no object: you lie down. The confusing part: the past of lie is lay.

meaning: to turn your eyes toward something on purpose
tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

meaning: to notice with your eyes
example: I can see the mountains from here.
tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

meaning: to look at something for a time, usually something moving
tip: See happens naturally. Look is short and on purpose (look at). Watch is longer, usually something that moves or changes.

meaning: to stop having something, or not win
tip: Lose has lost an o. Loose is "loooose", like a loose belt with extra room.

meaning: not tight or not firmly fixed
tip: Lose has lost an o. Loose is "loooose", like a loose belt with extra room.

meaning: to create or produce something
tip: Make is for creating something new (a cake, a plan, a mistake). Do is for tasks and activities (homework, the dishes, exercise).

meaning: to perform an action, task or job
example: I do my homework after dinner.
tip: Make is for creating something new (a cake, a plan, a mistake). Do is for tasks and activities (homework, the dishes, exercise).

meaning: belonging to or about one person
tip: Personal is about a person (stress on the first syllable). Personnel is staff (stress on the last syllable: per-son-NEL).

meaning: the people who work for an organization
tip: Personal is about a person (stress on the first syllable). Personnel is staff (stress on the last syllable: per-son-NEL).

meaning: the head of a school, or the most important
tip: The principal is your pal (the head of the school), and principal also means main. A principle is a rule (both end in -le).

meaning: a basic belief or rule
tip: The principal is your pal (the head of the school), and principal also means main. A principle is a rule (both end in -le).

meaning: making little or no noise
tip: Quiet ends in -et, like "silent" has a t. Quite ends in -te and changes how strong an adjective is.

meaning: fairly, or completely
tip: Quiet ends in -et, like "silent" has a t. Quite ends in -te and changes how strong an adjective is.

meaning: to keep something in your memory, or bring it back
tip: You remember something yourself. Someone else reminds you (remind needs a person after it).

meaning: to make someone remember something
tip: You remember something yourself. Someone else reminds you (remind needs a person after it).

meaning: to go up (no object)
example: The sun rises in the east.
tip: Raise needs an object: you raise something. Rise happens by itself: something rises.

meaning: to lift or increase something (needs an object)
tip: Raise needs an object: you raise something. Rise happens by itself: something rises.

meaning: to take money or things from a person or place illegally
tip: You rob a person or a place. You steal a thing. Thieves rob a bank and steal the money.

meaning: to take something that isn't yours
tip: You rob a person or a place. You steal a thing. Thieves rob a bank and steal the money.

meaning: to speak words
tip: You tell SOMEONE something, but you say something (TO someone). Tell usually needs a person after it.

meaning: to give information to someone
tip: You tell SOMEONE something, but you say something (TO someone). Tell usually needs a person after it.

meaning: practical and reasonable
tip: Sensible = good sense, practical. Sensitive = feels things strongly. (In many languages the word for sensitive looks like sensible.)

meaning: easily upset or affected; or understanding other people's feelings
example: She's very sensitive about her weight.
tip: Sensible = good sense, practical. Sensitive = feels things strongly. (In many languages the word for sensitive looks like sensible.)

meaning: from a point in time until now
tip: Since + a starting point (since Monday, since 2019). For + a length of time (for three days, for ten years).

meaning: showing a length of time
example: I've lived here for five years.
tip: Since + a starting point (since Monday, since 2019). For + a length of time (for three days, for ten years).

meaning: not moving
example: The car was stationary at the lights.
tip: Stationery with an e is envelopes and paper. Stationary with an a is standing still.

meaning: paper, pens and other things for writing
tip: Stationery with an e is envelopes and paper. Stationary with an a is standing still.

meaning: at that time, or next, after that
example: We had lunch and then went for a walk.
tip: Than is for compArison (both have an a). Then is for time (both have an e, like "when").

meaning: used to compare two things
example: She is taller than her brother.
tip: Than is for compArison (both have an a). Then is for time (both have an e, like "when").

meaning: in or at that place; also used to say something exists
tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

meaning: belonging to them
tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

meaning: short for "they are"
tip: There has "here" inside it (a place). Their has "heir" (someone who owns things). They're = they are.

meaning: toward a place, or before a verb
tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

meaning: also, or more than needed
tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

meaning: the number 2
tip: Too has an extra o: it means "extra" or "also". Two is the number. To is everything else.

meaning: going to other places in general
tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

meaning: going somewhere and coming back, usually for a short time
example: We took a trip to the mountains.
tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

meaning: traveling from one place to another, especially a long way
tip: Travel is the general activity (usually uncountable as a noun). A trip is a visit (there and back). A journey is the act of going from A to B.

meaning: if (used to talk about choices)
example: I don't know whether to go.
tip: Weather is about the sky (both have "ea" like "heat"). Whether is about a choice ("whether or not").

meaning: the conditions outside: rain, sun, wind
tip: Weather is about the sky (both have "ea" like "heat"). Whether is about a choice ("whether or not").

meaning: the person or people that (subject)
tip: If you can answer with he/she, use who. If you can answer with him/her, use whom (him and whom both end in m).

meaning: the person or people that (object, formal)
example: To whom should I send this?
tip: If you can answer with he/she, use who. If you can answer with him/her, use whom (him and whom both end in m).

meaning: belonging to which person
tip: If you can say "who is" or "who has", write who's. Otherwise it's whose.

meaning: short for "who is" or "who has"
tip: If you can say "who is" or "who has", write who's. Otherwise it's whose.

meaning: to get a prize or be first in a game or competition
tip: You earn money by working. You win a prize, a game or the lottery by luck or skill.

meaning: to get money for work
tip: You earn money by working. You win a prize, a game or the lottery by luck or skill.

meaning: belonging to you
tip: If you can say "you are" in the sentence, write you're. If not, write your.

meaning: short for "you are"
tip: If you can say "you are" in the sentence, write you're. If not, write your.
